requiredEdits.title: The new `UPDATE campaigns` bypasses the D2 source-mutation gate. Close it or record why it cannot bite.
requiredEdits.evidence: src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:477-483 writes the `campaigns` row directly. Every other writer of that table runs `evaluateSourceMutationGate` first: `saveCampaign` via `prepareCampaignWrite` (src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts:363 for the incoming record and :397 for the STORED one), and `storeReplicaCampaign` refuses `would-overwrite-source` at :208-211. `readCampaignSourceMarket` (:195-243 at HEAD) reads the row with no role check at all. requiredEdits.reachability: UNVERIFIED. requiredEdits.title: An offer that is an object but not a contract is either an untyped 500 or a malformed mission written into the source record.
requiredEdits.evidence: MEASURED this session with the temporary probe. (P1) With the stored market holding `offers: [{ "id": "contract-stored" }]` — an object, so it passes the new `storedOffers` guard, and `isContract` returns false at src/types/campaign/Mission.ts:384-396 so `rehydrateCampaignMission` leaves it untouched — the command reaches `computeCampaignStateDigest` and throws `EventJournalCanonicalizationError: JCS cannot represent undefined`, raised at src/lib/events/journal/EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts:40 through src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:414, UNTYPED, out of the prepared transaction. `validateCampaignIntent` does not stop it because `CONTRACT_MIN_STANDING = 0` (src/types/campaign/CampaignSync.ts:117) so `0 < 0` is false. (P2) With a contract-SHAPED offer whose `paymentTerms` is `{}`, the command COMMITS and the row gains `["contract-stored", { ... "paymentTerms": {}, "status": "Active" }]` — measured payload. Before this commit that shape only reached the journal-private envelope; now it is written into the source record as a mission.

axis1_transactionPlacement.singleImmediateTransaction: src/lib/events/journal/SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:112-136 — `this.db.transaction(() => { prepare(this.db); ...; extend(this.db, context, () => this.appendInTransaction(...)) }).immediate()`. One transaction wraps BOTH hooks on the SAME handle. `extend` receives `append` as a THUNK, so the caller chooses what runs after the append, still inside that transaction.
axis1_transactionPlacement.updateIsInsideAndAfterCommit: src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:454 `const appended = append();`, then the three refusal arms at :455-471, then `UPDATE campaigns SET payload = ?, version = ? WHERE id = ?` at :477-483. The UPDATE is reached only on `appended.kind === 'committed'`.
axis1_transactionPlacement.rowWithoutCommittedEvent: NOT REACHABLE by any arm read in this session. Every pre-append refusal (`source-record-absent` :363-365, `offer-absent` :369-372, the two rules refusals :380-405) returns from `prepare` before `append` is ever called. The three post-append refusals (`revision-conflict`, `command-identity-conflict`, non-`committed`) return before :477.
axis1_transactionPlacement.commitWithoutRow: NOT REACHABLE for a throw. The only statements between `append()` returning `committed` and the UPDATE are three `if` comparisons, which cannot throw. A throw from the UPDATE itself (disk-full, corruption) propagates out of the `.immediate()` transaction and rolls back the append with it — so the pair is atomic in both directions. Pinned by row (b), re-run green this session.
axis1_transactionPlacement.prepareStaysReadOnly: PASS. `prepare` only reads the row and COMPUTES the next payload (`nextSourceRecordAfterAccept` at :266-296, called at :424-428 into `IPreparedAcceptContext`); `extend` applies it. No write statement exists in the prepare callback. This honors the read-only contract documented at SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:83-97.
axis1_transactionPlacement.residualNote: `appendInTransaction` returns `committed` (via `hydrateBatch`, SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:175-182 → :275-277) for an IDEMPOTENT REPLAY — same commandId, same command digest — without writing any new event. The UPDATE would then fire and bump `version` on a command that wrote nothing new. Not reachable in the ordinary flow (after the first acceptance the offer is gone from the row, so `prepare` refuses `offer-absent` first, which is precisely what row (e) measures), and in the exotic case where it fires — a `campaigns` row restored behind a journal that kept the receipt — the write is arguably the correct repair. Recorded as a NON-BLOCKING observation, not a required edit.

axis2_rowFidelity.clientParity: VERIFIED against the client's own path, read this session. `acceptContractOffer` (src/stores/campaign/campaignCommandActions.ts:454-495) finds the offer in `contractMarket.offers`, refuses when `missions` already holds the id, calls `acceptContractEngine` and rebuilds the market. `acceptContract` (src/lib/campaign/contractMarket.ts:282-309) mutates exactly one thing: `{ ...contract, status: MissionStatus.ACTIVE }` appended to a copy of the missions Map. `serializeCampaign.ts:148` writes `Array.from(campaign.missions.entries())`, so the accepted pair lands LAST. `nextSourceRecordAfterAccept` (:266-296) produces the same three facts: prior entries under that id dropped, `[contractId, { ...storedOffer, status: ACTIVE }]` appended last, `offers` filtered by id, `declinedOfferIds` preserved. Match.
axis2_rowFidelity.serverIsStrictlyMorePreserving: The client rebuilds the market as `{ offers, declinedOfferIds }`, dropping any other key; the server spreads `...storedMarket`. `ICampaignContractMarket` (src/types/campaign/CampaignCommandExtensions.ts:38-44) has exactly those two fields, so today the two are identical and the server's form is the safer one.
axis2_rowFidelity.rawRoundTrip: PASS. `JSON.stringify({ ...storedRecord, version, body: nextBody })` — re-assigning an existing key inside a spread keeps its ORIGINAL position, so `version` and `body` do not move and every sibling key (`campaignId`, `schemaVersion`, `savedAt`, `originDeviceId`, `authority`, `instanceId`, anything else the envelope carries) round-trips byte-identically. One shape change: a body that carried NO `missions` key gains one at the end — unavoidable, and it is the field the acceptance changes.
axis2_rowFidelity.moneyFidelity: `Money.toJSON()` returns the plain amount (src/types/campaign/Money.ts:113) and `rehydrateMoney` accepts a number, a `{amount}`, a `{centsValue}` or a `Money` (src/lib/campaign/persistence/missionSerialization.ts:19-27). For a well-formed stored offer the client's rehydrate→re-serialize round trip is the identity, so the server's raw copy and the client's normalized copy agree byte-for-byte.
axis2_rowFidelity.versionAdvancedConsistently: PASS. Both the COLUMN and the envelope's own `version` move to `sourceRowVersion + 1` (:279, :291). That matches `saveCampaign`'s CAS semantics: the compare is against the COLUMN (src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts:110-113 and :126-131) and the envelope is what GET hands back, so a client that refetches after an acceptance gets a `baseVersion` the next PUT will win with. Test (a) asserts both, plus the stale-baseVersion 409, plus a cold reopen. Re-run green this session.
axis2_rowFidelity.denormalizedColumns: An acceptance changes none of `name`, `faction_id`, `campaign_date`, `balance` — correct to leave them. `saved_at` IS left stale: the row's payload advances but the column does not. Its only consumer is the campaign-list recency sort (`ORDER BY saved_at DESC`, CampaignPersistenceService.ts:282, backed by `idx_campaigns_saved_at`, SQLiteService.migrations.ts:345), so an authoritatively-accepted campaign does not move up the list. NON-BLOCKING; name it if the coordinator wants it closed.
axis2_rowFidelity.boundedDivergenceNote: For a DEGENERATE offer the two writers diverge: the client normalizes `paymentTerms` through `createPaymentTerms` (src/types/campaign/PaymentTerms.ts:257-270), which fills all seven keys from defaults, while the server copies the stored object raw. Measured in probe P2: `paymentTerms: {}` stays `{}` on the server path. Not reachable for a well-formed offer; folded into RE-2, which refuses the degenerate offer outright.
axis2_rowFidelity.mechanismVsDesignText: tasks.md:101 and design.md D13 (:139) describe the mechanism as '6.1's contract-only replay fold applied to the SAME commit'. `replayCampaignSourceContracts` (src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:220-249) produces `acceptedContracts` and `remainingMarket` but NO missions map and no next source body, so there was no existing function to reuse; the direct splice is new logic, not a duplicated fold, and using the RAW stored offer gives better byte fidelity than the fold's rehydrated form would. Reviewer judgement: the implementation satisfies the design's INTENT (one commit produces both projections) even though it does not literally call the fold. NON-BLOCKING, recorded so the divergence from the task text is not discovered later as a surprise.

axis3_behaviourChange_duplicateToOfferAb.verdict: PASS — acceptable under the spec; no consumer breaks today; 6.2b's client routing DOES need the note, and the note exists.
axis3_behaviourChange_duplicateToOfferAb.whatChanged: A same-actor identical re-submit used to answer `{ kind: 'duplicate', commandId }` from the command-identity arm; it now answers `{ kind: 'offer-not-durable', contractId, reason: 'offer-absent' }`, because `prepare` reads the reduced market before the append can consult the command log. Verified in red.log (received `{"commandId":"cmd-retry","kind":"duplicate"}`) and green at HEAD (row (e), re-run this session).
axis3_behaviourChange_duplicateToOfferAb.specJudgement: ACCEPTABLE. The requirement at spec.md:184-192 is about how many WRITES an acceptance produces, not about which vocabulary a retry is answered in; it says nothing about retry semantics, and the requirement's own text assigns the exactly-once obligation to the writer, which the implementer explicitly does not claim to discharge. Both answers mean 'nothing further was written', and row (e) additionally asserts the row is byte-identical after the retry. No SHALL is contradicted.
axis3_behaviourChange_duplicateToOfferAb.consumerSweep: MEASURED. `grep -rn "offer-not-durable|offer-absent|source-record-absent" src/ --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` excluding tests returns 9 hits and every one is a PRODUCER: campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts (:70, :72, :184, :352, :364, :371), campaignCommandPipeline.ts:165 (the union member), and src/pages/api/campaigns/[id]/commands.ts:208-217 (the 409 mapping). There is no consumer. Separately, no file under src/ outside `pages/api` issues a request to `/api/campaigns/[id]/commands` at all — the only two mentions are prose comments in campaignLifecycleState.ts:34 and :418 — so no client can observe the change today. Nothing breaks.
axis3_behaviourChange_duplicateToOfferAb.theHazardFor62b: The API route maps `duplicate` to HTTP 200 with the comment 'A retry is not a failure. The command committed once, which is exactly what the caller wanted' (commands.ts:157-164), and maps `offer-not-durable` to HTTP 409 with the comment 'The offer this command names has not reached the source record yet, which an acknowledged save fixes' (commands.ts:208-217). After this change, a same-actor retry of an acceptance that ALREADY COMMITTED takes the second path — and that path's advice is actively wrong for this case: saving and retrying will never make the offer reappear, because this actor consumed it. A 6.2b client that reads `offer-absent` as 'flush and retry' would loop.
axis3_behaviourChange_duplicateToOfferAb.doesTheNoteExist: YES, in three places: the implementer's evidence `observationsForTheNextSlice[0]`, commit B's message body, and the inline comment at the row (e) test. Reviewer recommendation (NON-BLOCKING, but do it): carry the same sentence into the 6.2b charter / brief so the next slice meets it as an input, since evidence JSONs are not what an implementer reads first. The tasks.md 6.2b text at line 101 currently states 'duplicate receipt lookup happens BEFORE the offer read' — which is no longer what the code does; that sentence is now stale and should be corrected when 6.2b is written (a tasks edit, correctly out of scope for this slice).
